title: PCOR-MII – Patient-Centered Outcomes Research as part of the Medical Informatics Initiative (MII) - Anorexia nervosa
summary: Anorexia nervosa has the highest mortality rate of any mental illness: around one in ten patients dies from the condition. It carries a high risk of becoming chronic, which has dramatic consequences for quality of life and social participation. This study therefore aims to identify the key factors that influence the progression of anorexia nervosa. In the long term, this should improve treatment outcomes for patients with anorexia nervosa. To this end, patients will repeatedly be surveyed over time regarding their current symptoms and limitations, as well as their current and past living conditions. Clinicians will also be asked for their assessments, particularly with regard to limitations caused by the disease. Blood and stool samples, as well as data from electronic patient records, will also be included in the analyses and interpretations.  This study forms part of the PCOR-MII initiative. Within this framework, the burden on patients of completing surveys is to be minimised by using a shortened selection of standardised questions.

interventions.name: No interventions are taking place. The study analyses and interprets prospective data from adult patients with ICD-10-GM diagnoses F.50.00, F50.01, F50.08 and F50.1 who are receiving outpatient, inpatient or day care treatment throughout Germany.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of Anorexia nervosa (ICD-10: F50.00, F50.01, F50.08, F50.1) 
- Consent may be obtained either through agreement to the broad consent framework or via consent to the study-specific information and consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute mental illnesses that require immediate further treatment (e.g., active suicidal ideation, acute psychotic state)
- Insufficient knowledge of the German language.
- Cognitive impairment that makes it impossible for the person to answer the questions adequately.
